sources.title: AWS Builders Library: caching challenges and strategies
sources.supportRationale: Measured cache value, modal failure behavior and origin protection.

sources.title: Microsoft Azure Architecture: cache-aside pattern
sources.supportRationale: Application-owned loading and invalidation order; example ordering does not eliminate every concurrent stale fill.

sources.title: Go x/sync: singleflight
sources.supportRationale: Per-Group duplicate in-flight function suppression; not a distributed ownership primitive.

sources.supportRationale: Shared/private storage, cache keys, validation and freshness semantics.

sources.title: Redis: persistence
sources.supportRationale: RDB/AOF durability and operational costs depend on configuration and failure model.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Trace slow requests by key class, result size, cache lookup, origin wait and fill work

scenarios.theme: The cache is empty and the origin cannot absorb full traffic. What is the recovery plan?
scenarios.assumptions: Normal traffic is 1,000 RPS with 50 origin reads/second. A restart removes the cache and origin capacity is 150 reads/second. What will you do?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Caching Fundamentals to cold origin capacity.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: The cache is empty and the origin cannot absorb full traffic. What is the recovery plan?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Admit bounded origin work, coalesce overlapping keys, prioritize useful warm-up and apply explicit degradation/refusal for excess demand

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Some users wait or receive reduced service; overprovisioning origin for full uncached load is another cost choice

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Unbounded retries can prevent recovery altogether.

scenarios.theme: A product lookup times out. Should you cache “not found”?
scenarios.assumptions: Repeated requests are expensive, but a transient origin failure cannot establish whether the item exists. What result do you store?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Caching Fundamentals to negative timeout.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A product lookup times out. Should you cache “not found”?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Keep failure distinct from authoritative absence, return an honest bounded error/degraded result and control repeated origin work separately

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Negative caching can protect the origin but delays visibility of newly created data; direct authoritative checks may suit correctness-sensitive reads

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Treating every exception as absence converts an availability fault into incorrect product state.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to aside, strategy; interview frequency is not claimed.
